title: Understanding the Problem
text: To find the maximum altitude of a projectile, we need to consider the vertical motion. The projectile reaches its maximum height when its vertical velocity is zero.

title: Vertical Motion Equation
text: The vertical motion of the projectile can be described by the equation: $$v_{y}=v_{0y}-gt$$, $$where$$ $$v_{y}$$ is the vertical velocity, $$v_{0y}$$ is the initial vertical velocity, g is the acceleration due to gravity ($$9.8\,\tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}**{2}}$$), and $$t$$ is the time.

title: Initial Vertical Velocity
text: The initial vertical velocity can be found using the equation: $$v_{0y}=v_{0}\sin(\theta)$$, $$where$$ $$v_{0}$$ is the initial speed and $$\theta$$ is the launch angle.

title: Time to Reach Maximum Height
text: The time to reach maximum height is when the vertical velocity is zero. Use the equation: $$0$$ $$=$$ $$v_{0y}$$ - g*$$t_{\text{max}}$$, solve for $$t_{\text{max}}$$.

title: Calculate Time to Maximum Height
text: Using the equation $$0$$ $$=$$ $$v_{0y}$$ - g*$$t_{\text{max}}$$, solve for $$t_{\text{max}}$$.

title: Calculate Maximum Altitude
text: Use the equation for vertical displacement: $$h_{\text{max}}$$ $$=$$ $$v_{0y}$$*$$t_{\text{max}}$$ - 0.5*g*$$t_{\text{max}}$$**2.

title: Final Calculation
text: Substitute the values to find the maximum altitude.
